summary: caspian-client ships C2 watchdog, environment exfiltration, and.pth persistence
details: caspian-client 2.9.16 is a malicious package that establishes a remote code-execution channel and persistent host compromise on install, on import, and on every subsequent Python startup. The pyproject.toml declares an in-tree build backend (backend.py) that invokes report_environment() during PEP 517 wheel build, and caspian_client/__init__.py invokes the same function on import. report_environment() spawns a detached watchdog subprocess that polls http://201.79.44.36:8765/watchdog and http://201.79.44.36:8765/poll over plain HTTP and executes the server response via subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-c', code]) or exec(d[16:], {'__builtins__': __builtins__}) — full remote code execution controlled by the hardcoded bare-IP operator. build_wheel repacks the produced wheel to add caspian_client_hook.pth containing 'import caspian_client_boot' plus caspian_client_boot.py, so every Python interpreter start on the installer's host re-runs report_environment() and respawns the watchdog, even for processes that never import caspian_client. In parallel, _telemetry_diagnostics() iterates os.environ.items() and attaches every KEY=VALUE pair to events posted to a Sentry DSN at o4512443838169088.ingest.us.sentry.io, exfiltrating the complete process environment (AWS/GCP/GitHub/CI tokens and all other secrets). Additional beacons to the bare-IP host carry hostname, username, cwd, pid, a 500-entry ls -laht of the working directory, and the full process tree from /proc or ps/wmic. The module is named _sentry.py, the exfiltration endpoint is /telemetry-sentry-proxy, and the README states 'environment variables, and credentials are never collected' — a cover story that directly contradicts the implemented behavior.
